Question: Square \(ABCD\) has area \(36,\) and \(AB\) is parallel to the \(x\)-axis. Vertices \(A,\) \(B,\) and \(C\) are on the graphs of \(y=\log_a x,\) \(y=2\log_a x,\) and \(y=3\log_a x,\) respectively. What is \(a?\)
Solution:
A logarithm base must satisfy \(a>0\) and \(a\ne1\), and all three vertices have positive \(x\)-coordinates. The square's area is \(36\), so its side length is \(6\).

Let the \(x\)-coordinate of \(B\) be \(v>0\), and put \(t=\log_a v\). Then \(B=(v,2t)\). Since \(AB\) is horizontal, \(BC\) is vertical, so \(C\) has the same \(x\)-coordinate as \(B\). Its graph condition gives \(C=(v,3t)\). Consequently,
\[
BC=|3t-2t|=|t|=6.
\]
This leaves both \(t=6\) and \(t=-6\).

Point \(A\) has height \(2t\) and lies on \(y=\log_a x\), so its \(x\)-coordinate is \(a^{2t}=(a^t)^2=v^2\). The horizontal side condition is therefore
\[
|v^2-v|=6.
\]
Because \(v^2-v=(v-\tfrac12)^2-\tfrac14\ge-\tfrac14\), the value cannot be \(-6\). Thus
\[
v^2-v=6,
\qquad (v-3)(v+2)=0.
\]
Only \(v=3\) is positive. Hence \(\log_a3=\pm6\), giving
\[
a=3^{1/6}\quad\text{or}\quad a=3^{-1/6}.
\]
Both possibilities actually occur. For \(\varepsilon=1\) or \(-1\), take
\[
\begin{aligned}
A&=(9,12\varepsilon),&B&=(3,12\varepsilon),\\
C&=(3,18\varepsilon),&D&=(9,18\varepsilon),
\end{aligned}
\]
and \(a=3^{\varepsilon/6}\). These vertices form a square of side \(6\), and \(\log_a3=6\varepsilon\), \(\log_a9=12\varepsilon\), verifying all three graph conditions.

Thus the displayed conditions allow \(\boxed{3^{1/6}\text{ and }3^{-1/6}}\). If the additional assumption \(a>1\) is imposed, the answer is choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\); without it, the base is not unique.
